source_observation.finding: ro_snapshot opens one read-only sqlite3 connection and performs separate SELECT statements for epoch, generation, tasks, scopes and leases without an explicit BEGIN or an explicit PEP-249 autocommit=False transaction boundary. The returned state_digest therefore lacks source-level proof that all fields were read from one SQLite read transaction snapshot.

external_method_evidence.finding: With the current default LEGACY_TRANSACTION_CONTROL, implicit transaction opening is tied to DML statements; other statements such as SELECT do not receive Python-level implicit transaction handling. PEP-249 autocommit=False is the recommended always-open transaction mode.

SQLite snapshot isolation is a property of a read transaction: once a read transaction starts it keeps an unchanging database snapshot, while a later new read transaction can observe newer committed state.

Different readers may have different WAL end marks; a particular reader's end mark is stable for the duration of its transaction. Same database file therefore does not by itself imply same snapshot identity across processes.

material_inference.claim: A future Popen/barrier repair can still be proof-insufficient if it only demonstrates simultaneous liveness and a shared database path. Each child must also establish a transaction-bounded observation, and the harness must prove that the ten observation identities are the same or otherwise explicitly define a valid evidence-rebase protocol.
not_claimed: No runtime interleaving failure has been observed in the current harness from this analysis alone.
No physical GRID10 component credit is minted.
No J-Space, HCU, EntityOS or training credit is minted.

hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Without an explicit read-transaction boundary, a concurrent writer can commit between ro_snapshot SELECT statements so the returned digest can combine fields from different committed states and fail to identify a real atomic observation snapshot.
hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: Current harness scheduling happens to prevent all writes during every ro_snapshot call, making the missing transaction boundary harmless in observed runs.
hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.cheapest_discriminator: Add a deterministic adversarial writer that advances a covered table/meta field between selected ro_snapshot reads. The old implementation must either produce a mixed-state witness or demonstrate a stronger invariant that excludes the interleaving. Then repeat with one explicit read transaction and require stable snapshot fields.

hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Ten simultaneously live Popen children can still observe different legitimate SQLite snapshots when their read transactions begin at different times around an S1 commit.
hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: A write-free barrier interval around all child snapshot acquisition is sufficient to make all ten observation identities equal without lower-level sqlite3_snapshot APIs.
hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.cheapest_discriminator: Preregister a barrier protocol: parent freezes S1 writers, children enter BEGIN/read transaction, emit PID plus epoch/digest plus ready marker, parent verifies all ten are alive and all identities equal before releasing the barrier; inject one controlled writer between two child BEGIN points as the negative control.

hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.hypothesis: SQLite URI mode=ro proves read-only opening intent but does not prove transaction-scoped atomic snapshot identity across multiple SELECTs or multiple processes.
hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.counterhypothesis: The surrounding Fabric protocol already freezes S1 strongly enough that mode=ro plus digest equality is operationally equivalent to the required proof.
hypotheses_and_counterhypotheses.cheapest_discriminator: Trace whether any S1 mutation is possible between child snapshot acquisition points under the exact harness protocol; if yes, require explicit transaction/barrier evidence.

minimum_requirements: Make each child observation transaction-scoped before the first covered SELECT and retain that read transaction until all snapshot fields are captured.
Prove ten distinct OS PIDs and overlapping liveness with a barrier or equivalent handshake.
Prevent or explicitly control S1 writes during the shared-snapshot acquisition window, or use an exact snapshot-identity mechanism with equivalent proof strength.
Receipt per-child PID, process start/ready/stop evidence, observation epoch/digest/generation and the barrier/freeze identity.
Add adversarial negative controls for writer commits between child transaction starts and between covered reads.
Bind the final runtime receipt to clean head/tree and exact source hashes; component PASS remains component-scoped.

next_exact_action: Before any new physical GRID10 execution pin, repair and regression-test both dimensions together: ten-process overlapping liveness and transaction-bounded same-snapshot acquisition. Do not treat Popen conversion alone as sufficient.
